title: Reconstruction from finite monoid coefficient quotients
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal such that $A	o\varprojlim_{j\ge1}A/I^j$ is bijective [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Let $P$ be a commutative additive monoid and $
u:P	o\mathbf N$ satisfy $
u(0)=0$ and $
u(u)+
u(v)\le
u(u+v)$. Assume $S_n=\{p\in P:
u(p)<n\}$ is finite for every $n\ge1$, and $\{(u,v)\in P^2:u+v=p\}$ is finite for every $p$. Let $R=A[P]$ be the monoid algebra of [def-trf-complete-toric-model] (zero polynomial variables), the ring of finite sums $F=\sum_p c_pz^p$, with $z^uz^v=z^{u+v}$, and let $J\subseteq R$ be an ideal satisfying, for every $n\ge1$,
$$F\in J^n\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad c_p\in I^{\max(n-
u(p),0)}	ext{ for all }p.$$
Ideal powers mean finite sums of products, with $I^0=A$. Put $\widehat R=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}R/J^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and let $\pi_n:\widehat R	o R/J^n$ be its projection. There is an $A$-algebra isomorphism $c:\widehat R	o A^P$, where $A^P$ has pointwise addition, convolution $(ab)_p=\sum_{u+v=p}a_ub_v$, and scalar embedding $a\mapsto az^0$. The isomorphism is required to satisfy the following coefficient condition, and is unique subject to it: if $x\in\widehat R$, $p\in P$, $j\ge1$, $N\ge j+
u(p)$, and $F_N\in R$ represents $\pi_N(x)$, then $c(x)_p$ modulo $I^j$ is the coefficient of $z^p$ in $F_N$ modulo $I^j$. For every $a=(a_p)\in A^P$ and $n\ge1$,
$$\pi_n(c^{-1}(a))=\left[\sum_{p\in S_n}a_pz^pight]\in R/J^n.$$
The canonical image of $az^p\in R$ is sent by $c$ to the family with coefficient $a$ at $p$ and zero elsewhere.

source.place: Exposé VI §1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70: agent-supplied coefficient refinement of the formal monoid models; not a verbatim theorem of ILO.

proof.text: For finite sums $F,G\in R$, the assumed criterion applied to $F-G$ gives $[F]=[G]$ in $R/J^n$ exactly when $F_p-G_p\in I^{\max(n-\nu(p),0)}$ for every $p$; here $F_p$ denotes the coefficient of $z^p$. If $x\in\widehat R$ and $F_N,F_M$ represent its levels with $M\ge N$, compatibility means $F_M-F_N\in J^N$. Hence their $p$-coefficients agree modulo $I^j$ whenever $N\ge j+\nu(p)$. Representatives at the same level also agree modulo $I^j$ under this bound. Two arbitrary eligible levels are compared through their maximum. These conclusions use just the stated criterion and the compatible-sequence definition [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion].

source.place: Tag 00M9 (section-completion), compatible-sequence description, and Tag 0317 (definition-complete). Agent argument using the coefficient criterion in the item; ILO Exposé VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70, motivates only the formal models.

proof.text: For each $x\in\widehat R$ and $p\in P$, let $r_{p,j}\in A/I^j$ be the $p$-coefficient of a representative at level $j+\nu(p)$, reduced modulo $I^j$. Step 1 makes this independent of the representative and of replacement by any larger eligible level. The residues are compatible as $j$ increases: use the representative at the larger level for both reductions. By the assumed bijection $A\to\varprojlim_j A/I^j$, there is a unique $c(x)_p\in A$ with these residues [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. This defines $c:\widehat R\to A^P$ and proves its required coefficient condition for every eligible $N$. The same injectivity shows that two elements of $A$ agreeing modulo every $I^j$ are equal.

source.place: Tag 00M9 (section-completion), compatible-sequence description, and Tag 0317 (definition-complete). Agent argument using the coefficient criterion in the item; ILO Exposé VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70, motivates only the formal models.

proof.text: For a family $a\in A^P$ put $T_n(a)=\sum_{p\in S_n}a_pz^p$, a finite polynomial by the assumed finiteness. For $m\ge n$, the difference $T_m(a)-T_n(a)$ is supported at $p$ with $n\le\nu(p)<m$. The criterion imposes only membership in $I^0=A$ at these positions; all other coefficients of the difference are zero. Thus $T_m(a)-T_n(a)\in J^n$. The classes $[T_n(a)]$ therefore define $d(a)\in\widehat R$ by [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and $\pi_n(d(a))=[T_n(a)]$.

source.place: Tag 00M9 (section-completion), compatible-sequence description, and Tag 0317 (definition-complete). Agent argument using the coefficient criterion in the item; ILO Exposé VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70, motivates only the formal models.

proof.text: For $N\ge j+\nu(p)$ with $j\ge1$, one has $p\in S_N$, so the $p$-coefficient of $T_N(a)$ equals $a_p$. Applying the coefficient condition from step 2 to $d(a)$ gives $c(d(a))_p\equiv a_p\pmod{I^j}$ for every $j$. Injectivity of the coefficient-completion map [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] gives $c(d(a))_p=a_p$ for all $p$, hence $cd=1$.

source.place: Tag 00M9 (section-completion), compatible-sequence description, and Tag 0317 (definition-complete). Agent argument using the coefficient criterion in the item; ILO Exposé VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70, motivates only the formal models.

proof.text:
Conversely let $a=c(x)$ and let $F_n$ represent $\pi_n(x)$. If $p\in S_n$, set $j=n-
u(p)\ge1$. The coefficient condition with $N=n$ gives $a_p-(F_n)_p\in I^{n-
u(p)}$. If $p
otin S_n$, the criterion at $p$ asks only for membership in $I^0=A$. It follows for every $p$ that the coefficient of $T_n(a)-F_n$ satisfies the criterion, so this difference lies in $J^n$. Thus $\pi_n(d(c(x)))=\pi_n(x)$ for every $n$. Equality of compatible sequences [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] gives $dc=1$. In particular $c$ is a bijection and $d=c^{-1}$, with exactly the asserted projection formula.

source.place: Tag 00M9 (section-completion), compatible-sequence description, and Tag 0317 (definition-complete). Agent argument using the coefficient criterion in the item; ILO Exposé VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70, motivates only the formal models.

proof.text:
Fix $p$ and $j\ge1$, and choose $N\ge j+
u(p)$. For every decomposition $u+v=p$, superadditivity and nonnegativity give $
u(u),
u(v)\le
u(p)$, so the same $N$ is eligible for all these coefficient residues. If $F_N,G_N$ represent $x,y$ at level $N$, their sum and product represent $x+y,xy$, since completion has componentwise operations [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Polynomial multiplication [def-trf-complete-toric-model] gives $(F_NG_N)_p=\sum_{u+v=p}(F_N)_u(G_N)_v$, with zero coefficients included outside the finite supports. The pair set is finite by hypothesis. Reduction modulo $I^j$ and the coefficient condition therefore give $c(xy)_p\equiv\sum_{u+v=p}c(x)_uc(y)_v\pmod{I^j}$; addition similarly gives $c(x+y)_p\equiv c(x)_p+c(y)_p$. As this holds for every $j$, injectivity of $A	o\varprojlim_j A/I^j$ [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] gives both equalities in $A$.

source.place: Tag 00M9 (section-completion), compatible-sequence description, and Tag 0317 (definition-complete). Agent argument using the coefficient criterion in the item; ILO Exposé VI 1.6(i)--(ii), printed p. 70, motivates only the formal models.

proof.text: The canonical image of a fixed polynomial $F$ is represented by $F$ at every level [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Its coefficient family under $c$ is therefore $(F_p)_p$, because its residues agree with those coefficients for every $j$ and the coefficient-completion map is injective [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Taking $F=0,1$ or $az^p$ proves preservation of zero and unit, the monomial formula, and preservation of the scalar embedding $a\mapsto az^0$. Together with step 6 and bijectivity, this makes $c$ an $A$-algebra isomorphism: the ring laws for the specified finite convolution follow by applying the bijection $c$ to the corresponding laws in $\widehat R$. Finally any other map satisfying the coefficient condition has the same residue at every $p,j$, hence the same coefficient by injectivity. This proves the required uniqueness.

Step 3: T_m-T_n is supported where the requirement is I^0=A, so d(a) is well defined. Step 4: j>=1 puts p in S_N, so cd=1. Step 5: j=n-nu(p) with N=n is eligible, so dc=1 and the projection formula holds. Step 6: superadditivity gives nu(u),nu(v) <= nu(p), the decomposition sum is finite, so c is multiplicative and additive. Step 7: unit delta_0, scalar a·delta_0, monomials; the ring laws transfer along the bijection c; uniqueness by injectivity. Small cases checked: P={0}; finite P with nu=0; P=N, I=0 gives A[[z]]; I=A forces A=0; Z/2. lean.statement: theorem filteredMonoid_coefficient_limit (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (I : Ideal A) [IsAdicComplete I A] (P : Type v) [AddCommMonoid P] (ν : P → ℕ) (hzero : ν 0 = 0) (hadd : ∀ p q : P, ν p + ν q ≤ ν (p + q)) (hfinite : ∀ n : ℕ, 1 ≤ n → Set.Finite {p : P | ν p < n}) (hpairs : ∀ p : P, Set.Finite {q : P × P | q.1 + q.2 = p}) (J : Ideal (AddMonoidAlgebra A P)) (hJ : ∀ (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∀ F : AddMonoidAlgebra A P, F ∈ J ^ n ↔ ∀ p : P, F.coeff p ∈ I ^ (n - ν p)) : ∃ (ring : CommRing (P → A)) (alg : @Algebra A (P → A) _ ring.toSemiring) (c : @AlgEquiv A (AdicCompletion J (AddMonoidAlgebra A P)) (P → A) _ _ ring.toSemiring _ alg), (∀ (a b : P → A) (p : P), (@Add.add (P → A) ring.toAdd a b) p = a p + b p) ∧ (∀ (a b : P → A) (p : P), (@Mul.mul (P → A) ring.toMul a b) p = ∑ᶠ q : {q : P × P // q.1 + q.2 = p}, a q.1.1 * b q.1.2) ∧ (∀ (a : A) (p : P), (@algebraMap A (P → A) _ ring.toSemiring alg) a p = if p = 0 then a else 0) ∧ (∀ (x : AdicCompletion J (AddMonoidAlgebra A P)) (p : P) (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → ∀ N : ℕ, j + ν p ≤ N → ∀ F : AddMonoidAlgebra A P, Ideal.Quotient.mk (J ^ N) F = AdicCompletion.evalₐ J N x → Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ j) (c x p) = Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ j) (F.coeff p)) ∧ (∀ (a : P → A) (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n), AdicCompletion.evalₐ J n ((@AlgEquiv.symm A (AdicCompletion J (AddMonoidAlgebra A P)) (P → A) _ _ ring.toSemiring _ alg c) a) = Ideal.Quotient.mk (J ^ n) (∑ p ∈ (hfinite n hn).toFinset, AddMonoidAlgebra.single p (a p))) ∧ (∀ (a : A) (p q : P), c (AdicCompletion.of J (AddMonoidAlgebra A P) (AddMonoidAlgebra.single p a)) q = if q = p then a else 0) ∧ (∀ d : @AlgEquiv A (AdicCompletion J (AddMonoidAlgebra A P)) (P → A) _ _ ring.toSemiring _ alg, (∀ (x : AdicCompletion J (AddMonoidAlgebra A P)) (p : P) (j : ℕ), 1 ≤ j → ∀ N : ℕ, j + ν p ≤ N → ∀ F : AddMonoidAlgebra A P, Ideal.Quotient.mk (J ^ N) F = AdicCompletion.evalₐ J N x → Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ j) (d x p) = Ideal.Quotient.mk (I ^ j) (F.coeff p)) → d = c)
